---
title: "Empty space around motifs"
subtitle: "Keep a ring around each motif, fill the rest"
---

## In plain words

Many Sjónabók motifs sit in a square with empty corners. Before the banner is
generated, a small extra step goes over each motif: it keeps the motif's own
stitches, a ring of background one stitch wide around them, and any holes the
motif closes in. The rest of the square is marked as *empty space*.

The fill method then treats that empty space like the gaps between motifs and
grows new pattern into it. The ring means the new pattern never touches the
motif, so the motif stays readable. Motifs that already fill their square are
left as they are.

In the text files the empty space is written as a dot, so the three states are
easy to see and edit:

```
..........00100..........
.........0010100.........
...0000001010101000000...
...0100110101010110010...
```

The knitted chart is still only background and stitch: empty space that is not
filled is knitted as background.

## The settings

**Ring width** is how much background is kept around each motif. A wider ring
leaves less empty space and a calmer banner.

## The banner

```{=html}
<div class="banner-viewer" data-method="clear"></div>
<script src="../js/banner-viewer.js"></script>
```

## Good at, weak at

| Good at | Weak at |
|---|---|
| More new pattern, without touching the original motifs | Only about half the motifs have empty space with a 1-stitch ring |
| Motifs stay readable because of the ring | The new pattern can look like a frame when the corner is small |
